paper_title: Parallel Bayesian Global Optimization of Expensive Functions
mechanistic_insights: The paper develops a parallel Bayesian optimization algorithm (MOE-qEI) for expensive-to-evaluate, derivative-free functions.
The core of the algorithm is the efficient maximization of the 'multipoints expected improvement' (q-EI) criterion.
A stochastic gradient estimator for the q-EI surface is constructed using infinitesimal perturbation analysis (IPA) and is shown to be unbiased.
The proposed MOE-qEI algorithm finds higher-quality solutions with fewer function evaluations compared to heuristic methods like Constant Liar (CL-mix).
The algorithm's computation time scales better with the number of parallel evaluations (q) than methods using closed-form q-EI formulas, particularly for q > 4.

quantitative_outcomes.notes: This is a computational methods paper from the field of Operations Research, not a synthetic chemistry paper. It describes a general optimization algorithm (MOE) that could be applied to chemical reaction optimization, but it contains no actual chemical data, reactions, or specific insights into cross-coupling. Performance is evaluated on mathematical test functions (e.g., Branin, Hartmann, Ackley), not chemical yields.
